subject: Executive briefing: p99 spike on long-context (32k) workflows — Medisync
messages:
From: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@medisync.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Medisync Platform Ops <ops@medisync.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes on 32k-window workflows — urgent

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a dramatic increase in p99 latency (and intermittent 500s) starting late last night for our clinical-summary pipeline that uses the 32k context endpoint on hosted.redwood. Throughput is fine but tail latency is causing timeouts in our downstream workers. We tried pinning to the same model version; behavior started at ~02:10 UTC.

Quick summary:
- p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 450ms, p99 jumped from 1.1s to 6.8s over the last 6 hours
- error rate increased from 0.2% to 2.6% (mostly 500s with "context overflow" or "kv-cache timeout")
- affected jobs are long-context: avg tokens in request ~ 18k, bursts of 28–32k tokens

We need an urgent mitigation — this is impacting our production processing window and will trigger SLA credits if not stabilized. I've attached a prom snapshot and a zipped set of traces. Can we get an immediate short call with your engineering and an exec-level touchpoint?

Attachments: prometheus_snapshot_20280328.json, p99_trace_2028-03-30.zip

Thanks,
Aaron
VP, Engineering
Medisync

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@medisync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:40:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on 32k-window workflows — urgent

Aaron — thanks for the level set and the artifacts. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra and looping in the account team + engineering leads for a cross-functional runbook.

Immediate plan:
1) We’ll triage traces and prometheus snapshot right away (Laura).
2) Temporary mitigation to limit concurrent 32k requests per tenant to reduce queueing (deploy within 3 hours).
3) If mitigation is insufficient, we’ll fallback matching requests to a lightly-quantized 24k-compatible variant to avoid KV-cache pressure (Grace).
4) Exec sync in 90 minutes to confirm SLA exposure and next steps.

Please expect a calendar invite from Marissa for an urgent 30-min sync. Laura — can you confirm whether we have sufficient trace coverage to pinpoint kernel-level stalls vs. routing backpressure? Marissa — I'll need a short mutual action plan PDF to share on the call.

Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@medisync.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:48:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on 32k-window workflows — urgent

Aaron — calendar invite sent for 10:30 PT (30 min). Attendees: Mina, Laura, Grace, myself, and your ops lead. I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out owner, ETA, and validation steps.

On the call we’ll cover: timeline of impact, immediate mitigation (rate limiting), short-term rollback/fallback, and estimated customer-facing timeline for full regression fix. If we agree on the MAP, I can draft an exec note for your CIO.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_0329.pdf

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@medisync.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:05:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on 32k-window workflows — urgent

Thanks for the context — I pulled the traces in p99_trace_2028-03-30.zip. Quick notes from triage:
- We see KV-cache hold times spiking on the 32k-path; there are multiple long mutex waits while eviction runs compete with active prefix fetches. That matches the "kv-cache timeout" signature Aaron mentioned.
- There are a handful of requests that grew to 32k tokens due to user-generated embeddings appended to long prompts; these hit an under-optimized attention kernel on the current build.
- No obvious network flapping; this looks local to runtime/kernel interaction under long-token pressure.

Immediate technical mitigations I can push now:
A) Tenant-level concurrency cap for requests >24k tokens (soft cap = 6 concurrent). Deploy as a config change and monitor.
B) Short-term on-the-fly fallback to the 24k-compatible quantized variant for requests that exceed 28k tokens but are tolerant to minor quality variance (configurable flag on the routed model).
C) Start a focused perf job to backport a KV-cache eviction pin that reduces mutex contention — ETA for PR: 5 business days, canary 48–72 hours after merge.

Requesting: full request ids for 20 of the p99 samples (I marked them in the trace bundle). Aaron — can your team send those request IDs and any user-level correlation ids? That will let us map to placement and kernel logs.

Laura Bennett
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@medisync.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mortem update & temporary mitigation roll-out

Team / Aaron — closing the loop on actions from the urgent sync. Summary and outcomes: 
- Temporary tenant-level concurrency cap (requests >24k) rolled out as a config change at 15:20 PT on 2028-03-30. Initial telemetry shows p99 reduced from 6.8s to ~1.3s for affected workflows; error rate fell from 2.6% to 0.3%.
- We enabled opt-in fallback routing for requests >28k to a quantized 24k-compatible variant for Medisync; alternating requests are tested in canary (10% traffic) now.
- Engineering (Laura) has opened INF-7891 for the eviction-contend fix; target PR by 2028-04-06 and canary 2028-04-09.
- We’ll provide a formal RCA and a timeline for the permanent fix by EOD 2028-04-04.

Attachments: p99_trace_2028-03-30.zip, prometheus_snapshot_20280328.json

Next steps for Medisync: please share 20 request_ids Laura requested and any correlation ids. Marissa will coordinate a customer exec note and timeline. Grace, I’ll schedule a follow-up exec readout next week.

Thanks everyone — Mina
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
